note: All player-facing text. Every line is placeholder wording written by the lab until the designer replaces it.

rows.text: The cabin is too run-down to enter. Still needed: {steps}.
You need the hammer in your backpack.
You don't have the materials for any repair step here.
The cabin is repaired. The door opens.
You are too tired for that.
You unfold the map and start surveying. Stand still...
You moved, so the survey stopped.
Surveying needs the map, compass and pencil in your backpack.
It is too dark to survey.
You can't survey in this weather.
From the outlook you can see for miles.
You add firewood to the stove.
You need firewood for the stove.
Go to sleep for the night? (Y / N)
Someone found you and brought you back to the station. They were gone before you woke.
Someone found you and brought you to the old cabin. They were gone before you woke.
This save was made by a newer version of the game and cannot be loaded.
This save file could not be read.
Beyond the gate, the road isn't open yet.
You aren't sure where you are.
The game saves only when you sleep. Quitting loses anything since then.

A note pinned to the board, in the last ranger's hand: "There's an old cabin out past the stream, northeast, by my reckoning. Roof's gone, door's off. If you ever fancy fixing it up, it'd make a fine place to sleep out there. I've marked roughly where on your map. The axe and bedroll in the chest are yours."
No jobs yet. Try the note board in the station.
Job added. Press J to see it.
You lay out the bedroll and light a small fire.
You need firewood to make camp.
You put more wood on the fire.
Sleep here by the fire for the night? (Y / N)
You wake stiff and a little cold, but rested. You roll up the bedroll and put out the fire.
You chop the tree down and get {n} firewood.
There's no tree close enough to chop.
You clear the {what} out of the way.
You dig out a stretch of trail.
You need the shovel to dig trail.
Click to make one. Esc to close.
You don't have what that needs.
You need the hammer to put that up.
A sign goes on a trail, or right beside one.
You put up a trail marker. (The hammer takes it down again.)
Everything is ready. Declare the {name} open? (Y / N)
Cabin holding up? Good. Past the pond our creek comes out of, there's an old fire tower. I put stakes in across the burn so I'd stop losing it. Follow the ribbons. Bring nails. More than that. - R.
Tower's dry and the radio works, mostly. The old road runs down off the hill to the river. The bridge was fine last time. - R.
Something new to look for. It's on your map, roughly.
Someone found you and brought you to the fire tower. They were gone before you woke.
From up here you can see for miles. The map fills in.
These reeds would twist into rope.
Hazelnuts and berries would make a good trail mix.
With rope and a few sticks you could make a frame for a bigger pack.
These mushrooms would make a good hot soup, with an onion.
Fiddleheads would fry up nicely with an onion.
Rose hips would steep into a warming tea.
This glowcap gives you an idea about your lantern.
This ember moss gives you an idea about your bedroll.
This sliver gives you an idea about your compass.
Glowcap. A small violet mushroom that gives off its own light. It only seems to show itself at night.
Ember moss. An orange moss on dead wood, warm to the touch, even in the snow.
Lodestone sliver. A splinter of dark stone that pulls at anything iron. The compass needle won't sit still near it.
Each dig lays one more tile
Surveys work at dawn and dusk
A chance of a double pick
Each dig lays one tile more again, for half the energy
Fallen trunks fall to one cut, and chopping gives double firewood
Surveys reach half as far again, and work in rain
Walk 15% faster off the trail, and tall grass no longer slows you
Repair steps take two actions, and a quarter fewer planks
Camp restores 10 more, and cooked food gives a quarter more
A better chance of a double pick, and bushes fruit again in two days
Sense magical ingredients nearby, and they come back twice as fast
Found {item}. It feels strange in your hand.
You scrape a little pine resin from the bark.
This pine has given its resin for now.
You need a lit stove or camp fire to cook.
You fit the new pack frame. The backpack has room for more now.
A workbench kit is set up inside a repaired cabin or tower without one.
You lay a stretch of boardwalk.
Boardwalk is laid on boggy ground or shallows.
You stack a small cairn. (The hammer takes it down again.)
The ember bedroll is warm without a fire.
A specialty is waiting to be chosen.
Click to make. K or Esc to close.
Two tables. Families come for it.
Six tent spots and a fire ring. Campers stay here.
Anglers come for it. Sells fishing permits.
A rail and a visitors' sign. Visitors may climb it by day.
Cleans up to 4 assigned bathrooms or trash cans each day.
Picks up litter along the trails, fills in badger diggings, and clears one storm-fallen trunk a day.
Has cleaned three lighthouses and a submarine. Won't say which was worst.
Marta folds her apron very neatly. "Call me if the submarine comes back."
Brings his own mop. Names it.
Dev and the mop leave together. The mop seems sad.
Pearl hands back her keys, already polished.
Says he can smell a full trash can from a mile off. Says it proudly.
Hank sniffs the air one last time. "You'll manage."
Studying moss, part time. Will clean for moss facts.
Juniper leaves you a list of moss facts. There are forty of them.
Whistles while working. Only knows one tune.
Ollie whistles his one tune all the way to the gate.
Can carry a fallen trunk on one shoulder and a coffee in the other hand.
Rosa shakes your hand and nearly takes it with her.
Not especially big. Nobody remembers why.
Big Tom waves. Still not big.
Likes litter-picking the way some people like fishing.
Wren pockets one last bottle cap on the way out.
Has walked every trail in the county twice, once backwards.
Cass walks off backwards, for old times' sake.
Owns a very good shovel and would like it to be appreciated.
Eli lets you hold the shovel, just once, before going.
Leaves the trail tidier than nature intended.
Bea straightens the welcome sign on her way out.
A troll badger has tipped over a trash can. It looks pleased with itself.
A troll badger is asleep in the bathroom. The bathroom is closed until further notice.
A troll badger raided a family's picnic. The family is annoyed. The badger is not.
A troll badger has dug a hole in the trail. A shovel would fill it.
The bathroom at {site} smelled like a swamp having a bad day.
Please clean the bathroom at {site}. Please. PLEASE.
Bathroom at {site} was a bit grubby. Not a complaint. OK, a small complaint.
Cleanest bathroom I've ever used outdoors. Would wash hands again.
Thank you for the bench. My knees thank you too.
Sat on a bench and watched a squirrel for twenty minutes. Best part of the trip.
Long walk to {site}! A bench on the way would be lovely.
Could there be a picnic area at {site}? We ate our sandwiches standing up, like horses.
A bathroom at {site} would be very welcome. Very.
Nowhere to put our trash near {site}. We carried it home. It's in the car now. Forever.
Some litter along the trail near {site}. Not ours! We checked.
Walked all the way to {site}. Worth every step and most of the blisters.
Slept under the stars at {site}. Woke up under them too. They're very persistent here.
Caught a fish, said sorry, let it go. Great dock.
Our guide knew every tree by name. Some of the trees seemed to know her too.
[A child's drawing of a round, grumpy animal in a bathroom. It is labelled MR. GRUMBLES.]
Something small and round ate our potato salad. It didn't even say thank you.
Thank you for finding us! We were only a little bit lost. OK, quite lost.
We got lost and spent the night in a hollow log. Lovely log. Better signs, please?
[A drawing of the ranger, very tall, standing next to a very small tree. Signed by Troop 9.]
We picked up {n} bits of litter for our badge! Can we have a badge from you too?
We sang round the campfire until the owls joined in. Sorry about the owls.
It rained. It's a forest. We get it. Still had fun.
Keep it up, Ranger. The park's in good boots.
Nice week. Don't forget to eat something that isn't beans.
Good work out there. I read every word of these, you know.
A quiet week. Quiet's allowed. The trees don't mind.
Ranger, I've had a letter about the bathroom at {site}. Two, actually. One was mostly underlined. When you get a moment.
Ranger, I'm hearing about troll badgers. Again. They come for the mess, you know. Always have.
Ranger! Visitors! Real ones, with sandwiches. Well done. I knew you'd open the place up.
First campers in years. They'll go home smelling of woodsmoke and tell everyone. Good.
Five hundred dollars in a week. Don't spend it all on nails. Spend most of it on nails.
Heard you found a lost party. Nobody stays lost for long on your watch. That's the job, really.
A whole week of clean bathrooms. I'm told it's never happened before. I'm told that by the bathrooms.
P.S. If the radio at the tower tells you anything odd, write it down. Humour me.
P.S. Don't go across the river just yet. Not because of anything. Just don't.
P.S. The old ranger used to leave the porch light on. I never asked who for.
P.S. If the pond seems to be looking at you, it's being friendly.
P.S. I'd visit, but you know how it is. Well. You don't. That's fine.
Supply catalog  -  {wallet} gold in the wallet
Not enough money in the wallet for that.
Yesterday's order is on the station's supply shelf.
A kit is waiting at its pad.
The Chief's weekly budget arrived: {n} gold.
They left a note asking {n} gold for their trouble. Fair enough.
Staff board  -  wages paid every seventh day
Nobody is looking for work just now.
Not enough money for everyone's wages. Some staff are taking the week off. No hard feelings.
Stakes and a flag: a pad for a {name}. Order a kit from the catalog at the station.
A kit for this {name} is on its way.
Take down the {name}? You get {n} gold back.
The {name} is taken down. {n} gold is back in the wallet.
You scrub the bathroom until it squeaks.
There's a troll badger asleep in here.
Among the litter: {thing}. You note it in the notebook.
That needs to go near a trail.
You'd better map this ground first.
You put down the {name}. (The hammer picks it up again.)
The fire ring is cold. Firewood would light it.
The sign on the cabin door says {mode}. Turn it round?
The old cabin is booked tonight, by {party}.
A note on the door: BOOKED TONIGHT, {party}. The bed and chest are theirs tonight. You can always camp outside.
Gift shelf: gift goods and berry preserve only
An empty gift shelf. You have a few ideas for things visitors might like.
No new cards in the suggestion box.
Pin a card to the job list?
You shoo the troll badger. It waddles off, grumbling.
Your first troll badger. You note it in the notebook.
Met a troll badger at {place}. Small, round, grumpy. Seemed to like the mess.
You fill in the badger's hole.
"Oh, thank goodness, a ranger!" They follow you back to the trail and set off home. They leave {n} gold as a thank-you.
Ranger, a party of {party} hasn't come back. Last seen near {place}.
A party of {party} is lost, last seen near {place}. Find them if you can.
The lost party turned up at the gate this morning, sheepish and fine.
{party}, last seen near {place}. They're somewhere in the circle on the map.
A letter from the Chief is on the station's note board.
New cards in the suggestion box at the gate.
No cards read yet. The suggestion box is by the kiosk at the gate.
Visitors in the park: {n} in {parties} parties
Ready sites visitors can reach: none yet
a guidebook to a different park
The scouts all wave at once.
an idea comes when you carry {item}
an idea comes when you look at the empty gift shelf
(at a lit stove or camp fire)
You gather {list}. Your backpack is full.
Too far from the {name} to count for it: put it within {n} tiles.
There is nowhere to put it down in here.
There's no room to put that down.
You put down {n} {item}. X to pick it up again.
Better keep that. Drop it instead if you must.
Drag to move. Drop or Trash below.

X: sleep at camp (the hammer packs it up)
X: pick up what you dropped

C: set this up inside a repaired cabin or tower

You pack up the camp and put out the fire.
Hammer: stand by a broken building or a kit
press X at it to map it
join it to the station's trail. Dig with the shovel; clear blocks with the saw or axe
repair it: hammer (C) at the door, with what it needs

Find a place worth opening: explore, and read the note board.
The gift shelf: put gift goods and berry preserve here. Visitors buy from it as they leave, and the gold goes in your wallet.
The suggestion box: visitors leave cards about their day. Read them to see what they want; a card that asks for something can be pinned to your jobs.
You know the way to the {name} now. Where a trail joins it, you can walk there from the map (M).
You can't walk there from here.
You walk the trail to the {name}.
Rangers on duty from dawn to dusk
Not taken: you chose the other one.
Something out there earns this one.
You got too cold and passed out.
Next time, when the red W bar runs low: go indoors, light a stove, or make camp with your bedroll and some firewood.
You ran out of energy and passed out.
Next time, when the yellow E bar runs low: eat something from your backpack, or head for a bed before it empties.
You stayed out too late and passed out.
Next time, be in a bed (or at your camp) before the day ends at {time}.
Find it: it's somewhere in the circle on your map
Map it: press X at it
Join it to the station's trail: dig with the shovel between the two flags on your map (about {n} tiles). Trail tiles must touch side by side, not just at the corners. Saw or chop anything in the way
Join it to the station's trail
Repair it: hammer (C) at its door. {list}
Put up a sign naming it, beside the trail within {n} tiles
Press X at it to declare it open
Every job is done. Look for new ones on the note board.
Open the workbench box ({n} of {m} slots used): made things go here when your backpack is full
You make a {item}. Your backpack is full, so it's in the workbench box.
at a lit stove or camp fire
A pile of stones that marks a spot on your map, even off the trail.
A blank sign to name a place; a site needs one before it can open.
Used to make the pack frame.
Food for the trail: plenty of energy, light to carry.
For repairs, signs, boardwalk and most workbench things.
For repairing roofs: the cabin's and the tower's.
Set it up inside a repaired cabin or tower to make things there too.
Lay it across bog or shallows to make trail where you can't dig.
Small markers to show the way along a trail.
Stands in for planks and nails when repairing, so you carry less.
A hot meal: lots of energy and some warmth.
A filling meal: lots of energy.
Keeps well, and sells on the gift shelf.
A warm snack: some energy and a little warmth.
Warms you up when you're cold.
Put it beside a trail: visitors stop to rest.
Put it near a trail: visitors stop to eat.
Put it near a trail and light it: a warm place for visitors.
A gift good for the gift shelf: visitors buy it.
A gift good for the gift shelf: visitors buy it.
A gift good for the gift shelf: visitors buy it.
A gift good for the gift shelf: visitors buy it.
A gift good for the gift shelf: visitors buy it.
Changes your lantern. What it does, you'll find out.
Changes your bedroll. What it does, you'll find out.
Changes your compass. What it does, you'll find out.
Hover tips say what X does at the thing under the mouse, and what C does with an item-bar slot. "First week only" shows them for the first {n} days of a game. Click to change.
(order it from the catalog at the station)
Map it: press X at its marker (a post or a cairn)
Press X at its marker (a post or a cairn) to declare it open
The {name} is joined to the station's trail! Its flags are off the map.
The trail to the {name} is broken. Its flags are back on the map.
Under the old papers: notes from the last ranger, about places out in the forest. Something to read when the station's shipshape.
Dusted. You can see the titles again.
You pick up the trash can. Its spot is marked by the gate.
Branch cleared. One more armful of firewood.
The snag comes down. Firewood, and a clear way.
The new valve warms up with a hum. The radio clears its throat.
Map it: X at its door
Repair the door, walls, roof and window
Join it to the park's trails
Put up a sign naming it
Declare it open: X at its door
There's an old cabin out past the stream, northeast, by my reckoning. Roof's gone, door's off. Fix it up and it'd make a fine place to sleep out there. I've marked roughly where on your map.
Map it: X at its marker post
Join it to the park's trails
Put up a sign naming it
Declare it open: X at its post
A sketch of the land round it
North of the fork, the trail climbs to a rock with the best view this side of the river. Bring a pencil. You'll want to draw it.
Map it: X at its cairn
Join it to the park's trails
Put up a sign naming it
Declare it open: X at its cairn
Our creek comes out of a pond somewhere up past the cabin. Never did find the name for it. Somebody ought to.
Map it: X at its door
Repair the stairs, floor, roof and windows
Join it to the station by trail, all the way
Put up a sign naming it
Declare it open: X at its door
Past the pond there's an old fire tower. I put stakes in across the burn so I'd stop losing it. Follow the ribbons. Bring nails. More than that.
Fit the valve: X at the tower's radio
The tower radio needs a valve. Good radio, that, if a little ahead of itself.
Map it: X at its post
A page of the last ranger's journal: "Bridge went in the spring melt. Somebody'll mend it one day. Not me, not this year."
A page of the last ranger's journal
The old road runs down off the hill to the river. The bridge was fine last time.
The bridge is out: a gap you can't cross. That's beyond you for now, and that's all right.
Tidy the station: the desk, the shelf, the boots
Clear the branch on the trail past the door
Set the trash can out by the gate's marker
Welcome, Ranger. The station's been empty a while, and it shows. Tidy it up, clear the branch on the trail, and set the trash can out by the gate. Take your time. The Chief
Pick up litter at the gate
Put out 2 trash cans by the kiosk
Put out a bench by the kiosk
A letter from the Chief: "Drove past the gate this morning. Looked like a park somebody cares about. Well done."
Visitors judge a park by its front door. A couple of trash cans and somewhere to sit would go a long way. The Chief
Put 10 firewood and 2 tins of beans in the cabin's chest
A chest with dry wood in it is the best welcome there is. Worth keeping one stocked.
Put 10 firewood and 2 tins of beans in the tower's chest
A chest with dry wood in it is the best welcome there is. Worth keeping one stocked.
Pick up litter across the meadow and gate
Clear 3 branches on the station trail
Winter's left its usual calling cards. A tidy-up before the crowds would be grand.
Put out 2 more trash cans at {place}, the busiest place
Summer's here, and so is everyone else. More cans, cleaner bathrooms, fewer letters to me.
Put 15 firewood in each open cabin's and tower's chest
The nights are drawing in. I'd rather you were warm out there.
Look in on each open cabin and tower
Cold week coming. Would you look in on the cabins? I worry about them, in my way.
Put up signs at the fork pointing to the cabin and the outlook
Point the Way at the Fork
Hikers will reach the fork and stand there scratching their heads. A sign or two would save them. The Chief
Saw through the three fallen trunks and clear the brush
Walk the trail: cabin to pond, joined
The pond joined to the park's trails
The old trail past the cabin gives out before the pond. Trees down, and a couple of stretches gone to grass. Not much work, all told.
Clear the brush in the west gap
Join the pond to the stake trail's middle
The last ranger's stakes still mark the way across the burn, and their old path is mostly there. Two gaps want digging, one each side of the middle. Do them in either order.
Clear the brush and snags in the east gap
Join the stake trail's middle to the tower steps
The tower joined to the park's trails
The last ranger's stakes still mark the way across the burn, and their old path is mostly there. Two gaps want digging, one each side of the middle. Do them in either order.
Saw through the fallen trunk and clear the brush
Join the tower to the bridge's west end
Trail travel to the bridge's end
The road down to the river is sound underneath. A tree, two weedy stretches, and it's a road again.
Talk to the troop leader: X beside them
Pick up 10 litter near their camp
A scout's drawing: a ranger, very tall, holding a very small bag of litter. "OUR RANGER" it says.
A scout's drawing, for the notebook
Dear Ranger, my troop is working on the Litter badge and they need a real ranger to see them do it. We are at the campground. - Troop Leader
The bathroom at {site} could use you and a mop. The Chief
Had a note about the bathroom at {site}. You know what to do.
{site}'s bathroom. Need I say more? The Chief
The cans at {site} are filling up. Best empty them before the raccoons do.
Bins at {site}, nearly full. The Chief
Someone's been busy at {site}. The bins say so.
A chance of a lost belonging
Visitors have been dropping things along the way to {site}. A walk with a bag would sort it.
Litter on the trail to {site}. The Chief
The way to {site} has picked up some litter.
{site} gets visitors and has hardly anywhere to put their rubbish. Two cans would help. The Chief
Folks at {site} keep asking where the bins are.
Nowhere to sit at {site}. A bench would be a kindness.
{site} could use a bench. The Chief
People stand about at {site}. Give them a seat.
Firewood at the {building}: nearly gone. The Chief
The {building} could use more firewood in the chest.
Clear the mess that drew it
A troll badger has moved in at {site}. Shoo it off, and tidy whatever drew it.
Something with stripes and opinions has taken over {site}.
A storm's put a tree across the trail to {site}.
Tree down on the way to {site}. The Chief
The trail to {site} has a tree lying on it.
A badger's dug up the trail near {site}. Fill it in before someone turns an ankle.
Diggings on the trail near {site}. The Chief
The trail by {site} has holes in it again.
Three trails meet at {junction} and nothing says where any of them go.
A pointer at {junction} would help. The Chief
People keep getting turned round at {junction}.
{site}'s name sign has gone. People like to know where they are.
No sign at {site} any more. The Chief
Put a name back up at {site}.
Put out a picnic table at {site}
Go to where they were last seen
Find them, and X beside them
The radio: {party} hasn't come back. Last seen near {place}. Probably fine. Probably.
Nothing on the clipboard. The forest's still there.
Keep your eyes open out there.
Nothing finished yet. Plenty of time.
Q/E tabs   W/S jobs   wheel scrolls   X follows a link   Esc closes
X or click to carry on
A fresh season. Nothing changed on the clipboard.
Trail travel along the glowing way.
You already had that: {n} gold instead
Seasonal: retires at the season's end
The catalog's in a drawer under the old papers. Get the station shipshape first.
The radio hisses and crackles. It wants a valve before it will say anything useful.
"You're the ranger! Troop, look sharp!" The scouts start picking up litter with great ceremony.
{who} did it first: half pay, {n} gold.
B opens the book. J opens the clipboard.
Thank you, Ranger! It's just what the place needed.
A high place with a view?
ROAD CLOSED FOR REPAIRS, says a sawhorse across the town road. The station needs you first anyway.
The road to Humdrum is open. There's a letter from the chief at the station.

Ranger,

The county crew finished the town road yesterday, so the gate's open both ways now. Humdrum would like to meet its new ranger. Wren at the Percolator says the first coffee's on her.

Don't let them talk you out of the woods.

The chief
Through the gate and down the road: Humdrum.
The Humdrum notice board. A lost glove, a lost cat (found), the Thaw Fair's date, and a card that says: "Odd jobs? Ask in person." Favors will be pinned here soon.
{name} looks at the {item} for a long moment.
A birthday gift! {name} is delighted with the {item}.
That's not something to give away.
{name} has had two gifts this week already.
{keeper}: "We're closing up now. Come back tomorrow!"
Order from the supply catalog (arrives at the station tomorrow)
{name} isn't behind the counter right now.
Nothing in your backpack that {name} buys.
You have the {item} at a table. {effect}
Rosa slides a second plate across: "On the house."
The coffee kicks in: you walk faster for a while.
{name} is out. A note on the counter says: "Back soon! Leave the money in the jar."
Your backpack is full: no room for the {item} you'd take off.
Repairs what's broken, builds a kit at its pad, and takes down what you've put up.
Light to walk by after dark.
Fills in as you walk. Use it out on the trail to survey.
For marking the map. Surveying needs it.
Makes camp anywhere: a bed and a small fire for the night.
Wrapped in wax paper this morning.
Burns in a stove, a campfire or a fire ring.
Sawn boards, for repairs and building.
Shingles for a roof that leaks.
A pane for an empty window frame.
Cuts through a fallen trunk across the trail.
Digs new trail, and fills a hole a badger dug.
Put it up at a junction so people know the way.
A post that shows where the trail goes.
Everything a small repair needs, in one bundle.
Picked in the shade. The safe kind.
Sticky and fragrant, scraped from pine bark.
Glowcap. A small violet mushroom that gives off its own light. It only seems to show itself at night.
Nuts and dried fruit for the trail.
Kindling, and useful for making things.
Long and tough. They twist into rope.
Bright red, full of seeds. Good in tea.
Ember moss. An orange moss on dead wood, warm to the touch, even in the snow.

Put it down to build a workbench.
A lantern that never needs fuel.
A bedroll that keeps you warm without a fire.
A compass that seems to know more than north.

Put it down where litter gathers.
Put it down at a good spot for lunch.
Put it down for a safe campfire.
A spare valve for the fire tower's radio.
A card with flowers pressed into it. A nice gift.
Smells of the forest. A nice gift.
A little figure carved from pinecones. A nice gift.
A stone painted in park colours. A nice gift.
A soft glow for a dark room. A lovely gift.
Hot and strong. A spring in your step for a while.
The bakery's muffin of the day.
Eggs, beans and toast: a proper start.
Wrapped in corn husks, still warm.
A big bowl of hominy stew.
Teo's notebook of songs. He'll want it back.

Someone in town is missing these.

Sol painted the pond for you.
Pip drew you. You're taller in the drawing.

Worn as your {slot}. Drag it onto that slot to wear it.
